items.q: See, they had Earl Warren, they had Jack Washington, Herschel and Lester.

ctx.x: Most of the time he was playing alto?
Right. Alto and baritone. See, they had Earl Warren, they had Jack Washington, Herschel and Lester.

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sometimes we’d just start it on the bandstand and just pass it along. That’s how “One O’Clock Jump” was originated. Jack Washington is the one that set the riff

ctx.x: And who decided at what point that riff would start during a performance?

Usually, after Prez would take two or three choruses, then we’d set a riff behind him. Sometimes we’d just start it on the bandstand and just pass it along. That’s how “One O’Clock Jump” was originated. Jack Washington is the one that set the riff, (sings) boop e doo, bee doo dee doo dee doodle doo, and there was beee dah da da, (etc. singing) he was the first one to set that kind of riff, period. And then the trombone would say “boooooo, beee doodle (etc.)” Nobody could write that, nobody could even think about…
That same phrase was on a record earlier, a McKinney’s Cotton Pickers.
